A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PermuCATE study. Their main text, equations, figures, notation table, and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original simulation and semi-synthetic IHDP experiments comparing PermuCATE with LOCO, including supplementary risk-comparison and grouping analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds simulations with non-Gaussian covariates in Appendix A.13.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and Equation 4 retain the same conditional residual permutation, risk difference, normalization, and averaging procedure. Changes to the theoretical statements do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Appendix A.13 adds a synthetic scenario with non-Gaussian, multimodal covariates generated through nonlinear latent-variable transformations. The existing LD, HL, HP, IHDP, and grouped-variable scenarios remain.

E2.justification: LOCO remains the individual-variable comparator and LOGO the grouped comparator. Figure S6 reuses Figure 2's Ridge, CateNet, and TabPFN learner configurations. The expanded knockoff and CRT discussion introduces no evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Figure S5 adds distribution diagnostics using marginal densities, kurtosis against a Gaussian reference, and correlations. Figure S6 otherwise follows Figure 2's evaluation design. Existing splits, cross-fitting, permutation counts, learner settings, and performance metrics are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A.13 tests whether PermuCATE's variance advantage persists with more complex conditional covariate distributions, supported by Figures S5–S6. Existing risk-choice, finite-sample, dimensionality, and grouping analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Figure S5 newly reports a diagnostic labeled 'Kurtosis test' comparing generated and Gaussian covariates, without specifying a significance threshold or p-values. Existing simulation counts, Nadeau–Bengio testing, and Monte Carlo/bootstrap uncertainty reporting remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Figure S6 adds variance curves under non-Gaussian inputs, generally favoring PermuCATE, especially for nonlinear CATEs. Figure S5 adds distribution diagnostics. The eight earlier result plots are retained with unchanged plotted results; these additions are not same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: The central finite-sample bias result is substantially revised: Proposition 3.4 adds a linear CATE estimation-error term and places the Lipschitz-based bound in a new corollary. Proposition 3.2 and Appendix A.3 also correct the Sobol-index normalization. However, Appendix A.4 still concludes with the older covariate-error-only bound, leaving the revised statement incompletely reconciled with its proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and concluding discussion retain the same main contributions: adapting CPI to CATE, analyzing finite-sample variance, and demonstrating lower variance and greater statistical power than LOCO.

C2.justification: v3 acknowledges that IHDP cannot directly verify Assumption 3.1 and proposes that complex covariate distributions make both conditional estimation and CATE estimation harder. It also explains the newly retained linear CATE-bias term and distinguishes individual type-I error control from knockoff multiple-testing control.

D1.justification: Appendix A.13 documents the new simulation recipe: Gaussian-mixture latent variables followed by nonlinear transformations with interactions. Exact generator parameters remain unspecified. Existing learner implementation and hyperparameter information is unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Williamson et al. (2021) and expands positioning relative to Sobol/ANOVA interpretations, model-X knockoffs, and CRT, discussing estimands, guarantees, assumptions, and computational cost. Most other reference changes update existing works' publication metadata.

P1.justification: The overall organization and most prose remain. v3 adds Related Work and Problem Setting subheadings, shortens the roadmap, edits terminology and grammar, and updates affiliations and publication information. It also adds acknowledgments and funding/employer disclosures.

P2.justification: v3 adds Figures S5–S6, enlarges several existing appendix plots, renames Figures 5–8 as S1–S4, and relocates figures as text reflows. The main visual style, algorithm display, and notation table are retained.

improvement.justification: The added non-Gaussian robustness experiment and clearer distinctions from knockoffs and CRT provide useful empirical support and interpretation beyond v2. The Sobol normalization correction also helps. These gains are limited by the failure to reconcile revised Proposition 3.4 with Appendix A.4, leaving an important theoretical consistency problem unresolved.
